name: Bernardo Provenzano
milestone_by_age_26: Participated as one of 14 gunmen in the murder of Corleone Mafia clan leader Michele Navarra in August 1958 at age 25, consolidating Luciano Leggio's control of the Corleonesi.
early_history_summary: Provenzano left school at 10 to work in the fields and joined the Mafia as a teenager with his friend Salvatore Riina, becoming muscle for mob boss Luciano Leggio in cattle-rustling operations. He was known as an excellent shot and earned the nickname 'The Tractor' for his ruthless determination.
family_context_summary: Born to farming parents Angelo Provenzano and Giovanna Rigogliuso in Corleone, Sicily; third of seven children, left school at 10 to work in the fields during WWII.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Corleone mafia culture, poverty, early criminal activity, Leggio mentor, Riina peer
evidence_summary: Provenzano was born into a poor farming family in Corleone, Sicily, and left school at 10 to work in the fields during the Allied invasion of 1943. He joined the Mafia as a teenager along with his friend Salvatore Riina, becoming muscle for mob boss Luciano Leggio in cattle-rustling operations. In August 1958 at age 25, he was one of 14 gunmen who helped Leggio murder Corleone clan leader Michele Navarra, a pivotal event in his criminal career. His trajectory was shaped by growing up in Corleone, a town synonymous with Mafia activity, and by early immersion in the local criminal ecosystem under Leggio's mentorship.
starting_point: Born in Corleone, Sicily to farming parents; third of seven children, left school at 10 to work in the fields during WWII.
current_position: Died July 13, 2016 at age 83 in a Milan prison hospital; de facto boss of Cosa Nostra from 1993 to 2006, captured after 43 years as a fugitive.

trajectory.event: Participated as one of 14 gunmen in the murder of Corleone clan leader Michele Navarra, consolidating Luciano Leggio's control.
Became a fugitive after an arrest warrant was issued for murder; began 43 years on the run.
Became second-in-command of the Corleonesi under Salvatore Riina after Leggio's imprisonment.
Took over as de facto boss of Cosa Nostra after Riina's arrest.
Captured by police near Corleone after 43 years as a fugitive.
Died in a Milan prison hospital on July 13, 2016.

name: Pavel Pavel
milestone_by_age_26: Conducted a local practice experiment with a 12-tonne concrete model in 1982 at age 25, but his major recognition came at 29 when invited by Thor Heyerdahl to Easter Island in 1986.
early_history_summary: Studied electrical engineering at the university in Plzen and worked as a design engineer at Agrostav Strakonice; began experimenting with megalith transport methods as a hobby, conducting his first practice experiment with a 12-tonne concrete model in 1982 at age 25.
family_context_summary: Born as an only child to Ruzena and Ladislav Pavel in Strakonice; parents took him camping and on nature trips from a young age, and he was active in a scouting and water sports group.
evidence_summary: Pavel's interest in ancient transport methods began in childhood, and he studied electrical engineering in Plzen before working as a design engineer. His first practice experiment in 1982 at age 25 used a 12-tonne concrete model but was a local endeavor without wide recognition. His material milestone came in 1986 at age 29 when Thor Heyerdahl invited him to Easter Island to test his theory at full scale.

name: Mauri Kunnas
milestone_by_age_26: Working as a political cartoonist for Finnish newspapers by 1976, but his first published book collection (1978) and first children's book (1979) came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Graduated from the University of Art and Design in Helsinki as a graphic designer in 1975 and began working as a political cartoonist for Finnish newspapers including Aamulehti, Turun Sanomat, and Suomen Kuvalehti; created the Nyrok City rock and roll parody comic starting in 1975.
family_context_summary: Born in Vammala to Martti Kunnas and Martta Lastunen; graduated from Vammala High School in 1969.
evidence_summary: Kunnas graduated from the University of Art and Design in Helsinki in 1975 and began working as a political cartoonist for multiple Finnish newspapers. By age 26 he was a working professional, but his first published book collection (Jauhot suuhun, 1978) and first children's book (Suomalainen tonttukirja, 1979) came after age 26. His famous Koiramaki series began in 1980 when he was 30.

name: Lalo Schifrin
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 in 1958, completed Gillespiana (an extended suite for Dizzy Gillespie's big band), won Argentina's Academy award for the film score to El Jefe, and led a 16-piece jazz big band on Buenos Aires television.
early_history_summary: Schifrin began piano study at age six under Enrique Barenboim and later studied with Olivier Messiaen at the Paris Conservatory from age 20, playing jazz in Paris clubs at night. After returning to Argentina in 1956, he formed a 16-piece jazz big band on Buenos Aires television and met Dizzy Gillespie, who offered him a path to the US. By 1958 at age 26, he had completed Gillespiana for Gillespie and won Argentina's Academy award for a film score.
family_context_summary: Born in Buenos Aires to a musical family; father Luis Schifrin was concertmaster of the Buenos Aires Philharmonic at the Teatro Colon for three decades.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional violinist and concertmaster, providing direct musical domain exposure and training from age six.
primary_early_advantage_tags: musical family, father concertmaster, conservatory training, early piano study, Dizzy Gillespie connection
evidence_summary: Schifrin grew up in a highly musical household in Buenos Aires, with his father serving as concertmaster of the Buenos Aires Philharmonic for three decades. He began piano study at age six under Enrique Barenboim (father of Daniel Barenboim) and later studied at the Paris Conservatory with Olivier Messiaen, while simultaneously playing jazz professionally in Paris clubs. By his mid-20s he had performed with Astor Piazzolla at an international jazz festival, formed Latin America's first jazz orchestra (a 16-piece band on Buenos Aires TV), and met Dizzy Gillespie, who offered him a path to the US. At age 26, he completed Gillespiana for Gillespie and won Argentina's Academy award for a film score. His family's deep musical lineage and elite conservatory training provided exceptional early domain depth.
starting_point: Born in Buenos Aires to a musical family; father Luis Schifrin was concertmaster of the Buenos Aires Philharmonic at the Teatro Colon for three decades.
current_position: Died June 26, 2025 in Los Angeles at age 93; five-time Grammy winner and six-time Oscar nominee, received Honorary Academy Award in 2019; composed scores for over 100 films and TV shows.

trajectory.event: Performed with Astor Piazzolla and represented Argentina at the International Jazz Festival in Paris.
Met Dizzy Gillespie during his State Department tour of Buenos Aires; Gillespie offered him to come to the US.
Completed Gillespiana suite for Dizzy Gillespie and won Argentina's Academy award for his film score to El Jefe.
Moved to New York City and joined Dizzy Gillespie's quintet as pianist and arranger.
Composed the iconic theme for Mission: Impossible television series.
Scored the film Bullitt, cementing his reputation in Hollywood.
Received an Honorary Academy Award for his career achievements.
Died in Los Angeles on June 26, 2025.

name: Adriana Karembeu
milestone_by_age_26: Discovered by a French modeling agency in 1994 at age 23, but her breakthrough Wonderbra campaign came in 1998 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Enrolled at Charles University in Prague to study medicine; was discovered by a French modeling agency in 1994 during her third year of studies after competing in a beauty pageant, leading her to leave Slovakia for a modeling career in Paris.
family_context_summary: Born in Brezno, Czechoslovakia to a Czech engineer father and Slovak doctor mother; parents were both students at the time of her birth, so she was raised by grandparents until age six.
evidence_summary: Karembeu was studying medicine at Charles University in Prague when she was discovered by a French modeling agency in 1994 at age 23 after competing in a beauty pageant. She began modeling professionally, but her material breakthrough, the Wonderbra campaign, came in 1998 at age 27. At 26, she was a working model without a major campaign to her name.

name: Tamara Bunke
milestone_by_age_26: Moved to Cuba in 1961 at age 24 after being personally recruited by Che Guevara, and participated in the Cuban literacy campaign and the Federation of Cuban Women.
early_history_summary: Bunke grew up in a Marxist-Leninist household in Buenos Aires where her parents' home was used for communist meetings and hiding weapons. She joined the Free German Youth at 15 after the family returned to East Germany, and was recruited as an interpreter for the Socialist Unity Party, where she met Che Guevara in 1960.
family_context_summary: Born in Buenos Aires to German communist parents who fled Nazi persecution; father Erich was in the Communist Party of Germany, mother Nadia was a Russian Jewish communist.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were communist activists and teachers, providing direct ideological and political domain immersion from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: communist parents, political household, Free German Youth, Che Guevara, Cuba
evidence_summary: Bunke was born in Buenos Aires to German communist parents who fled Nazi persecution; both were teachers and Communist Party activists whose home was used for meetings, helping refugees, and hiding weapons. She joined the Free German Youth at 15 after the family returned to East Germany, and was recruited as an interpreter for the Socialist Unity Party, where she met Che Guevara during his 1960 visit to Leipzig. In 1961 at age 24, she moved to Cuba and participated in the literacy campaign and Federation of Cuban Women, directly entering the revolutionary project. Her parents' deep ideological commitment and political networks provided the foundation for her revolutionary career.
starting_point: Born in Buenos Aires to German communist parents who fled Nazi persecution; father Erich was in the Communist Party of Germany, mother Nadia was a Russian Jewish communist.
current_position: Died August 31, 1967 at age 29 in Bolivia; revolutionary guerrilla fighter known as 'Tania', killed during Che Guevara's Bolivia expedition.

trajectory.event: Met Che Guevara during his visit to Leipzig while working as an interpreter for the Socialist Unity Party.
Moved to Cuba and participated in the Cuban literacy campaign and the Federation of Cuban Women.
Sent by Che Guevara on an underground mission to Europe under the alias 'Tania'.
Joined Che Guevara's guerrilla expedition in Bolivia.
Killed on August 31, 1967, in an ambush at the Rio Grande in Bolivia.

name: Eugenio Castellotti
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Mille Miglia and 12 Hours of Sebring with Ferrari in 1956 at age 25, having already won the Portuguese Grand Prix (1952) and debuted in Formula One with Lancia (1955).
early_history_summary: Castellotti acquired a Ferrari 166 at age 20 with family wealth and began racing in 1951, taught to drive by the family chauffeur. He won the Portuguese Grand Prix in 1952 at age 22, finished second at Monaco, and was signed by Lancia for their Formula One program in 1954.
family_context_summary: Born to a wealthy family in Lodi, Italy; father Francesco was a lawyer who wanted Eugenio to pursue law.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, Ferrari at 20, Italian motorsport ecosystem, Lancia works team, Alberto Ascari mentor
evidence_summary: Castellotti was born into a wealthy Italian family in Lodi; his father was a lawyer who wanted him to pursue law, but Eugenio was obsessed with motor racing from childhood and was taught to drive by the family chauffeur. He acquired a Ferrari 166 at age 20 with family wealth and began racing immediately, winning the Portuguese Grand Prix at 22 and breaking into Formula One with Lancia at 24. His family's financial resources enabled early access to elite racing machinery, and the Italian motorsport ecosystem provided a direct pipeline to works team drives with Lancia and Ferrari.
starting_point: Born in Lodi, Italy to a wealthy family; father Francesco was a lawyer who wished his son to pursue the same profession.
current_position: Died March 14, 1957 at age 26 in a testing accident at Modena; final role: Ferrari Formula One and sportscar driver, winner of the 1956 Mille Miglia and 12 Hours of Sebring.

trajectory.event: Began racing career with a Ferrari 166 in the Giro di Sicilia.
Won the Portuguese Grand Prix and finished second at the Monaco Grand Prix for sports cars.
Debuted in Formula One with Lancia; took maiden podium at the Monaco Grand Prix.
Won the Mille Miglia and 12 Hours of Sebring with Ferrari.
Died on March 14, 1957, in a testing accident at the Modena Autodrome.

name: Francisco Rodriguez
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in light flyweight at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics at age 23, becoming Venezuela's first Olympic gold medalist; also won Pan American Games gold in 1967 at age 21.
early_history_summary: Rodriguez started boxing at age 11 at a local gym in Cumana, then moved to Caracas for advanced training and joined the Venezuelan national team. He won gold at the 1967 Pan American Games at 21 and Olympic gold at 23 in 1968, compiling an amateur record of 266 wins and 4 losses.
family_context_summary: Born in poverty in Cumana, Venezuela; second of 14 siblings, raised by his grandmother, sold fish as a child and did not receive formal education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: extreme poverty, early boxing at 11, national team, self-made, 266 amateur wins
evidence_summary: Rodriguez grew up in extreme poverty in Cumana, Venezuela, as the second of 14 siblings; he did not receive formal education and sold fish with his grandmother as a child. He started boxing at age 11 at a local gym, then moved to Caracas for advanced training and joined the national team, compiling an amateur record of 266 wins and 4 losses. His trajectory was driven by early specialization and poverty-driven urgency rather than family resources, culminating in Pan American Games gold at 21 and Olympic gold at 23, making him Venezuela's first Olympic champion.
starting_point: Born in poverty in Cumana, Venezuela; second of 14 siblings, raised by his grandmother, sold fish as a child and did not receive formal education.
current_position: Died April 23, 2024 at age 78 in Caracas; Venezuela's first Olympic gold medalist, inducted into Venezuelan Sports Hall of Fame in 1988.

trajectory.event: Won gold at the Pan American Games in Winnipeg, claiming his first major international title.
Won Olympic gold in light flyweight at Mexico City, becoming Venezuela's first Olympic gold medalist.
Won gold at the Pan American Games in Cali, Colombia, his second Pan Am title.
Carried Venezuela's flag at the Munich Olympics opening ceremony; eliminated in first bout.
Inducted into the Venezuelan Sports Hall of Fame.
Died on April 23, 2024, in Caracas.

name: Ecaterina Oancia
milestone_by_age_26: Was on the Romanian national rowing team by her early 20s, but her first World Championship medal came in 1981 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Started in kayaking before being told she was too young and then too small to row; became a coxswain at her local club and joined the Romanian national team within two years of settling into the role.
family_context_summary: Born in Sangeorgiu de Padure, Romania; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Oancia started in kayaking before being redirected to rowing as a coxswain due to her small stature. She joined the national team within two years of taking up coxing, but her first international medal, a World Championship bronze in the coxed quad sculls, came in 1981 at age 27. Her Olympic gold followed in 1984 at age 30.

name: Aida Touma-Suleiman
milestone_by_age_26: Was politically active and held a degree from University of Haifa by her mid-20s, but founded Women Against Violence in 1992 at age 28, her first major organizational milestone.
early_history_summary: Born in Nazareth to an Arab Christian family; attended St. Joseph's School and earned a B.A. in psychology and Arabic literature from the University of Haifa before becoming involved in political activism and joining the Hadash party.
family_context_summary: Born into an Arab Christian family in Nazareth; attended St. Joseph's School in Nazareth.
evidence_summary: Touma-Suleiman earned a B.A. in psychology and Arabic literature from the University of Haifa and was politically active in her early career. However, her material milestone, founding the feminist organization Women Against Violence, came in 1992 at age 28. She was elected to the Knesset in 2015 at age 51.

name: Patrik Cavar
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold with Croatia at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics at age 25, having already won Mediterranean Games gold (1993), European Championship bronze (1994), and World Championship silver (1995).
early_history_summary: Cavar entered the senior handball squad of his hometown club RK Mehanika Metkovic at age 15, playing in the Yugoslav Second League. He moved to top-tier RK Borac Banja Luka at 17 and then to Badel 1862 Zagreb at 19, progressing through the elite Yugoslav handball pipeline to the national team.
family_context_summary: Born in Metkovic, Croatia (then part of Yugoslavia); family background not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yugoslav handball pipeline, senior debut at 15, Zagreb club, national team system
evidence_summary: Cavar began his handball career at his hometown club RK Mehanika Metkovic, entering the senior squad at age 15 and playing in the Yugoslav Second League. He moved to top-tier RK Borac Banja Luka at 17 and then to Badel 1862 Zagreb at 19, progressing through the elite Yugoslav handball pipeline. By his mid-20s he was a key player for the Croatian national team, winning Mediterranean Games gold, European bronze, World silver, and Olympic gold at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics. The Yugoslav/Croatian handball system provided an elite performance pipeline that accelerated his development, though family background details are not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Metkovic, Croatia (then part of Yugoslavia); family background not well documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired professional handball player living in Croatia; Olympic gold medalist (1996), former top goalscorer of the Croatian national team, two-time European club champion with RK Zagreb and three-time with FC Barcelona.

Won bronze at the European Handball Championship in Portugal with Croatia.
Won silver at the World Handball Championship in Iceland with Croatia.
Won Olympic gold with Croatia at the Atlanta Olympics; became top goalscorer of the national team.
Signed with FC Barcelona; won three European Cups over four years with the club.
Retired from professional handball in July 2007.

name: Liam Neeson
milestone_by_age_26: Joined the Lyric Players' Theatre in Belfast in 1976 and the Abbey Theatre in Dublin in 1978 at age 26, with a minor film debut in Pilgrim's Progress (1978); his breakout role came with Excalibur in 1981 at age 29.
early_history_summary: Born in Ballymena, Northern Ireland; was a youth heavyweight boxing champion before studying at Queen's University Belfast and a teachers' training college; joined the Lyric Players' Theatre in Belfast in 1976 and the Abbey Theatre in Dublin in 1978.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class Catholic family in Ballymena, Northern Ireland; father was a primary school caretaker and mother was a cook.
evidence_summary: Neeson was a youth boxing champion in Northern Ireland before joining the Lyric Players' Theatre in Belfast in 1976 and the prestigious Abbey Theatre in Dublin in 1978 at age 26. He made a minor film debut in Pilgrim's Progress (1978), but his breakout role in Excalibur (1981) came at 29, and his major recognition with Schindler's List (1993) at 41.
